kyr_otabi_hanten.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Read from both sides of the shop's printed お献立表, photographed at full resolution, March 2025.

items.en: Soy-sauce ramen
items.note: The plainest bowl in the house and the cheapest way in. Adding butter to any ramen here is +¥50.

items.en: Salt-seasoned ramen
items.note: Clearer and lighter than the soy version — same noodles and stock, different tare.

items.en: Miso ramen
items.note: Thicker and sweeter. Note that miso itself is sometimes barley-based (麦味噌) on top of the wheat noodles.

items.en: Ramen loaded with extra roast pork slices
items.note: The standard upgrade at any Japanese ramen shop: same bowl, the surface covered in pork.

items.ja: 御旅ラーメン（ピリ辛あんかけ麺）
items.en: House ramen — noodles under a mildly spicy thickened gravy
items.note: ピリ辛 = gently spicy, not punishing. あんかけ = the glossy starch-thickened sauce, which keeps the bowl scalding hot far longer than it looks.

items.en: Ramen topped with a crab omelette in sweet-sour gravy
items.note: 天津 (Tenshin/Tianjin) on a Japanese Chinese menu always means a fluffy egg omelette with crab stick under a thick sweet-vinegary sauce.

items.en: Nagasaki-style noodles with pork, seafood and cabbage, soy version
items.note: Everything stir-fried then simmered together with the noodles in one bowl — vegetables, squid, pork, fish cake. A meal in itself.

items.ja: 皿うどん（揚げ麺五目あんかけ）
items.en: Crisp fried noodles under mixed seafood-and-vegetable gravy
items.note: Despite the name it is not udon — it is a nest of thin deep-fried noodles that go soft where the sauce lands and stay crunchy elsewhere. Eat fast.

items.ja: 炸醤麺（ジャージャーメン）
items.en: Noodles topped with a salty minced-pork miso
items.note: Zha jiang mian — boiled noodles under a dark, intensely savoury meat-and-bean-paste sauce. Stir it all through before eating.

items.en: Stir-fried wheat noodles
items.note: Add ¥200 for 大盛り (oomori, large) on any noodle dish here.

items.en: Plain steamed white rice
items.note: Plain unseasoned rice — genuinely gluten-free and vegan. Ask for it not fried and with no sauce and it is the one safe order in the building.

items.en: Fried rice
items.note: Soy-seasoned, with egg and pork through it.

items.en: House rice bowl — pork, vegetables and egg stir-fried over rice
items.note: The dish the shop is known for and the reason locals come. Pork, cabbage, carrot, onion, wood-ear and egg in a soy-and-oyster-sauce glaze, poured over a very large amount of rice. Portions here are famously enormous.

items.en: Mixed stir-fry in thick gravy over rice
items.note: 八宝菜 = 'eight treasures': pork, squid, prawn, cabbage, carrot, quail egg and so on in a starch-thickened sauce, ladled over rice.

items.en: Crab omelette over rice with sweet-sour gravy
items.note: A Japan-invented Chinese dish, and a comfort-food benchmark — a soft egg blanket over rice with a glossy, slightly sweet vinegared sauce.

items.en: Mapo tofu over rice
items.note: Numbing-spicy tofu and pork mince on rice.

items.ja: 天津焼めし（塩あんかけ）
items.en: Crab omelette over fried rice with a salt-based gravy
items.note: The house mash-up: tenshin on top of fried rice instead of plain rice, with the clear salty gravy rather than the sweet one. Rice bowls are +¥200 for 大盛り (large).

items.en: Chinese set meal — crab omelette, mixed stir-fry and fried chicken with rice
items.note: Three mains on one plate plus a mountain of rice, for under ¥1,000. A blogger described needing a serious appetite to finish it.

items.en: 'Student set part 1' — crab omelette and Genghis-Khan mutton
items.note: The menu really does run 学生定食 parts I, II and III, all ¥950 — a relic of feeding hungry students. Part II is fish fry with pork-egg-vegetable stir-fry; part III is crab omelette with pork-and-cabbage miso stir-fry.

items.en: House set meal — sweet-sour pork, crab omelette and fried chicken
items.note: The greatest-hits plate. Three of the kitchen's best dishes side by side with rice.

items.en: Chinese bento A — sweet-sour fried chicken, crab omelette, shumai
items.note: 弁当 here is a compartmented lacquer tray, not a takeaway box. B (¥1,400) swaps in grilled pork loin; C (¥1,500) has tonkatsu and beef-and-aubergine.

items.en: Pan-fried pork dumplings
items.note: Startlingly cheap. Wheat skins, soy in the filling, soy-vinegar dip — the classic celiac trap dish.

items.en: Steamed open-topped pork dumplings
items.note: Thin wheat wrapper gathered around a pork-and-onion filling, steamed rather than fried.

items.en: Boneless fried chicken
items.note: 骨なし = boneless; the menu also lists 骨付き (bone-in) at the same price. Choose by how much work you want to do.

items.en: Whole-fried chicken under sweet-vinegar sauce
items.note: The menu glosses it itself: 鶏素揚げ甘酢がけ — chicken deep-fried undredged, then drenched in sweet vinegar sauce.

kyr_ramen_henteko.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Read from a photograph of the touchscreen ticket machine whose own clock reads 2025/07/17.

items.en: HOW TO ORDER: buy a ticket from the machine just inside the door, then hand it over at the counter
items.section: はじめに / Before you order
items.note: It is a touchscreen machine with photographs, a Language button in the top right, and an eat-in / takeaway toggle. Pick your bowl, press 発券 (hassuken) to print the ticket, take your change. Extra toppings added later at your seat are paid in CASH at the counter, not on the machine.

items.en: House soy-sauce ramen on a rich chicken-paitan broth
items.note: The shop's flagship and the one to order first. Chicken feet plus small bones and aromatics simmered about six hours into a thick, creamy 鶏白湯 (tori-paitan), finished with a soy tare. The owner trained at Meimon, ancestor of Kyoto's famously heavy kotteri style.

items.en: Salt version of the house chicken-paitan ramen
items.note: Same six-hour chicken broth, salt tare instead of soy — sweeter and more directly chicken-flavoured.

items.en: Chicken-paitan ramen boosted with fish powder and bonito oil
items.note: The shop's own best-seller. An in-house blend of dried-fish powder and katsuo (bonito) oil stirred into the soy bowl — creamy and oceanic at once, with a deliberately retro set of toppings.

items.en: Chicken-paitan ramen with roasted dried-sardine paste
items.note: Niboshi roasted then ground into a house paste — bitter, dark and concentrated, cut by the creamy chicken base. Served with flat noodles rather than the usual round ones.

items.en: Old-style clear soy noodle soup
items.note: The opposite of the paitan bowls: several kinds of chicken bone, several dried fish and dried shiitake drawn out slowly at low temperature into a clear 清湯 (chintan) soup, with a slightly sweet house soy kaeshi and thin springy noodles. Topped with chashu, menma, negi and — rare in Kansai — なると (naruto, the pink-swirled fish cake).

items.ja: のすたるじっく冷やし中華
items.en: 'Nostalgic' cold Chinese-style noodle salad
items.note: Summer only. Chilled noodles with cucumber, egg and pork in a tart dressing — the flavour Japanese adults associate with childhood summers.

items.en: Limited special A — the rotating experimental bowl
items.note: 限定 (gentei) = limited. The owner is a restless experimenter, so there is nearly always a 限定A and 限定B on the machine and no way to know in advance what they are — look at the posters on the wall by the door. Past ones: chilled mapo ramen, sake-lees ramen, a Jiro-style prawn-miso bowl, a carbonara bowl. Sells out.

items.en: Limited special B — second rotating bowl
items.note: Usually the pricier of the two limiteds. A red SOLD OUT overlay appears on the machine when it is gone — often by early afternoon.

items.en: Chilled mapo ramen — an example of a recent 限定A
items.note: House chilli oil and mapo mince over a cold soy-milk base with medium-thick curly noodles — ¥1,200 for 150g of noodles. Shown here as an example of what the 限定 slot looks like; it will not always be on.

items.ja: 墨染テコ系らーめん（泡）
items.en: House take on iekei ramen, foamed version — a recent limited
items.note: ¥1,200 for 150g of noodles, ¥1,300 for 220g. Thick chicken-paitan soy with spinach, wood-ear, naruto and the house chashu, whipped to a foam. Another example of the rotating limiteds.

items.en: Large noodle portion
items.note: +¥100 for the large. On the 魚介, 煮干し and 限定 bowls the surcharge is paid in cash directly at the counter, not on the ticket machine.

items.en: Extra spring onion
items.note: 増 (mashi) = 'more of'. The cheapest way to change a bowl.

items.en: Extra fermented bamboo shoot
items.note: メンマ is bamboo shoot lacto-fermented then simmered — crunchy and sour-savoury. The simmering liquid is soy-based.

items.en: Extra roast pork slices
items.note: Braised pork, sliced. Soy-braised, so out on both counts.

items.en: Soy-marinated soft-boiled egg
items.note: Jammy yolk, steeped in soy tare. The universal ramen add-on — you will see 味玉 or 煮玉子 on almost every ramen menu in Japan.

items.en: Kimchi
items.note: Japanese kimchi often contains fish sauce or salted shrimp.

items.ja: 替え玉（定番しょうゆ・塩）
items.en: Refill of noodles, for the standard soy or salt bowls
items.note: 替え玉 (kaedama) means a second nest of noodles dropped into your remaining broth — the Kyushu habit, adopted widely. Leave enough soup. Order it at your seat and pay cash. For any bowl other than the standard soy or salt it is ¥150.

items.en: Lunch set: 2 pieces of fried chicken plus a medium rice
items.section: ランチタイムセット / Lunch sets (11:00-14:30)
items.note: Choose トリ唐 (tori-kara, plain fried chicken) or ヒリ唐 (hiri-kara, the spicy one), or a half-and-half. Upgrading the rice from 中 (medium) to 大 (large) is +¥50. Available 11:00-14:30 only.

items.en: Lunch set: a small rice bowl alongside your ramen
items.section: ランチタイムセット / Lunch sets (11:00-14:30)
items.note: Pick one of three: 炙りチャーシュー丼 (blowtorched pork over rice — wasabi on the side, ask them to leave it off if you would rather), ネギ塩レモンチャーシュー丼 (with salted spring onion and lemon), or カルボTKG (a carbonara-ish raw-egg rice).

items.ja: 卓上調味料（おろしにんにく・一味・コショウ・唐揚げの塩・七味）
items.en: On-table seasonings: grated garlic, chilli powder, pepper, seasoned salt for the fried chicken, seven-spice
items.note: Free to use. The garlic paste is what regulars stir into the paitan bowls. 一味 (ichimi) is pure chilli; 七味 (shichimi) is the seven-spice blend with citrus peel and sesame.

kyr_ramen_viska.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Taken from the shop's own blog and its newest wall boards, August 2026. A 2024 board circulating online prices the kotteri ¥100 lower and still shows the old Jiro call system — it is obsolete.

items.en: WHICH BOWLS ARE ON TODAY: check before you go
items.section: はじめに / Before you order
items.note: This is a one-man counter of 7 seats in a converted snack bar. The kotteri-based bowls (こってり, ビス郎, 汁無) are made on an irregular schedule because of prep constraints, while あっさり and クリアビス郎 run every open day. The owner posts the exact list for each stretch of days on his own note blog and on X/Instagram — worth a look the morning of. Sells out early on some days.

items.ja: こってり（超超濃厚豚骨）
items.en: Ultra-thick pork-bone ramen
items.note: ¥1,050 for 並 (nami, regular, 150g of noodles), ¥1,150 for 大 (dai, large, 225g). The shop's headline bowl and genuinely one of the thickest tonkotsu broths in a city that specialises in thick broths — closer to gravy than soup, clinging to medium-thick straight noodles. こってり literally means rich or heavy; あっさり is its opposite.

items.ja: あっさり（透き通る豚骨）
items.en: Clear, light pork-bone ramen
items.note: ¥1,100 regular (150g), ¥1,200 large (225g). Two aged raw soy sauces from long-established Kyoto makers blended into the tare, plus kombu and bonito dashi and Okayama chicken. Comes with chashu, house-made wontons and spring onion. There is yuzu in it — say so when ordering if you dislike citrus.

items.en: Thick chicken-and-pork paitan ramen
items.note: ¥1,200 regular (150g), ¥1,300 large (225g). The signature of the owner's previous shop, brought back — runner-up in the chicken-paitan category of the 2018 Kansai Ultimate Ramen Award. The price includes an ajitama; ¥100 off if you do not want it. Contains yuzu.

items.ja: 極濃煮干し中華そば（限定）
items.en: Limited: extra-concentrated dried-sardine soy ramen
items.note: ¥1,150 regular (150g), ¥1,250 large (225g), ¥1,050 mini (75g) — the mini is a rare and useful option if you want to try two things. Toppings for this bowl: 2 extra wontons ¥100, extra pork ¥300, extra onion ¥50. The shop recommends its 和え玉 (ae-dama) — a pre-seasoned second nest of noodles you eat separately rather than dropping into the soup.

items.en: House Jiro-style ramen — a mountain of beansprouts, cabbage, back-fat and pork over very fat noodles
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: ¥1,200 for 並 = 300g of noodles. IMPORTANT and unusual: this shop is コール不要 — you do NOT have to shout the Jiro call. At a standard Jiro-style shop staff ask ニンニク入れますか (garlic in?) and you answer with some combination of ニンニク (garlic) / ヤサイ (extra veg) / アブラ (extra back-fat) / カラメ (stronger seasoning), plus 少なめ (less), マシ (more), マシマシ (loads). Here garlic, veg and fat are all self-service at the counter — take what you like. Noodle weight can be tuned in 10g steps at ±¥10 per 10g, with no upper limit.

items.en: Brothless Jiro-style — the same pile with no soup
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: 汁無し = no soup. Sauce and oil sit at the bottom; mix hard from underneath before eating.

items.en: Lighter Jiro-style bowl
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: ¥999 for 300g of noodles — same size, gentler build, and the cheapest full bowl in the shop. Promoted from trial to regular menu in July 2026.

items.en: Brothless lighter Jiro-style
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: The soupless version of the Light, added July 2026 at the same price.

items.en: 'Clear' Jiro-style — the same pile on a clean, non-kotteri soup
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: One of the few bowls available every open day, because it does not use the kotteri stock. On the older board it was priced at +¥100 over the corresponding Bisurou size; confirm the current price at the shop.

items.en: Chilled brothless Jiro-style with pork and mayo
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: A summer-only addition on the August 2026 rotation. Price not published in the sources found.

items.ja: 本格スパイスカレー汁無（ビス郎）
items.en: Limited: proper spiced-curry brothless Jiro-style
items.section: マシマシ系（二郎系）/ Jiro-style
items.note: ¥1,400 for 300g. A rotating limited — on the wall when it is on.

items.en: The everything topping — extra pork, extra spring onion and a marinated egg
items.note: Common to こってり and あっさり. This is the shop's 全部のせ (zenbu-nose, 'put it all on'). On 濃厚とりとん the equivalent is called 特製 and also costs ¥600.

items.en: Extra pork
items.note: マシ (mashi) = more. The pork is a shoulder-cut chashu; for a stretch of 2026 it was made from named Shonan Miyaji-buta pork.

items.en: Extra spring onion
items.note: Raw sliced green onion, to cut the fat of a very heavy bowl.

items.en: Soy-marinated soft-boiled egg
items.note: Already included in the price of 濃厚とりとん.

items.ja: 無料トッピング（高菜・紅生姜・無限ニンニク）
items.en: Free toppings: pickled mustard greens, red pickled ginger, bottomless garlic
items.note: Help yourself at the counter. 無限ニンニク literally means 'infinite garlic'. A fourth free item, 赤ガッパ (a chashu-offcut relish), was suspended indefinitely in July 2026. Takana and beni-shoga are usually seasoned with soy and sometimes contain fish extract.

items.en: A bowl of plain rice, self-service
items.note: One bowlful, taken yourself from the rice cooker — not free refills. Plain unseasoned rice, so genuinely gluten-free and vegan on its own. The shop is fussy about its rice and names the producer on its blog.

items.en: Suntory black oolong tea, bottled
items.note: The standard bottled tea; unsweetened and slightly bitter.

items.en: Sapporo beer, 500ml bottle
items.note: Not served to anyone driving a car or motorbike.
